syllabus_topics: Introduction to the quantum model of the atom
Chemical bonding in diatomic molecules - Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT)
Chemical bonding in polyatomic molecules - Valence Bond Theory (VBT)
Intermolecular forces and properties of covalent compounds
Polymers: Structure and morphology. Polymerization reactions
Metals: Structures. Metallic bonding according to MOT: Band theory and Cohesion Energy. Metallic alloys
Covalent crystals - Bonding according to MOT: Band theory
Introduction to electrical properties: Conductors, Semiconductors, and Insulators
Fundamentals of Chemical Kinetics and Thermodynamics
Applications to the engineering course in question
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 0.3*T + 0.2*L + 0.5*E, where T is the average of 3 tests, L is the laboratory worksheet, and E is the exam. A minimum score of 7 out of 20 is required for the exam. Students pass if NF is 9.5/20 or higher. For resit exams (ER), NF = 0.2*L + 0.8*ER or NF = 0.3*T + 0.2*L + 0.5*ER, taking the best of the two. Special conditions apply for late admissions, working students, high-performance athletes, re-enrolled students, and grade improvements.
